inbodydescription.para: Validate ECC params pointer.
Validate input addresses provided.
Validate that exactly one of KeyAddr or KeyId is provided, and that a vault sourced key carries no length.

briefdescription.para: This function validates ECC parameters for public key generation.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS, if ECC parameters are validated successfully.
XASU_INVALID_ARGUMENT, if parameter validation fails.

inbodydescription.para: Validate input parameters.
Validate that exactly one of PvtKey.KeyAddr or PvtKey.KeyId is provided, and that a vault sourced key carries no length.

Validate curve information. When key is provided via address, both CurveType and KeyLen are validated. When KeyId is used (vault-stored key), only CurveType is validated since the firmware derives key length from the stored key metadata.

listitem.para: XST_SUCCESS, if ECC parameters are validated successfully.
XASU_INVALID_ARGUMENT, if parameter validation fails.

inbodydescription.para: Validate input parameters.
Validate that a destination for the shared secret is provided.
Validate the metadata the shared secret is stored under: the selected vault shall be within the supported range, and the secret is only ever stored in the KDF/HMAC sub-vault.
Validate that exactly one of PvtKey.KeyAddr or PvtKey.KeyId is provided, and that a vault sourced key carries no length.
Validate that exactly one of PubKey.KeyAddr or PubKey.KeyId is provided, and that a vault sourced key carries no length.

When the shared secret is written to client memory, SharedSecretLen must be at least the curve shared-secret length. For an address-sourced private key that is KeyLen. For a vault-sourced key KeyLen is 0 here; ASUFW rechecks against the length from key metadata after vault resolution.
Both keys must use the same curve.

Validate curve information. Since both keys share the same CurveType, only one range check is needed. For each key provided via address, both CurveType and KeyLen are validated; vault-stored keys (KeyAddr == 0) skip KeyLen validation since the firmware derives it from metadata.
